title: What is/are the best AI model(s) for C++ and UE5 mainly?
author: TheHoppingGroundhog
selftext: i wanted to try out using an AI to aid wherever it can to make my own game, but don't know where to start. i really, really don't want to have to pay a subscription.

comments.author: ianxplosion-
comments.body: Well you’re probably going to have to pay a subscription

comments.author: Katwazere
comments.body: If you have a decent pc then you may be able to run qwen3 locally(the coder varient is yet to appear on ollama), but unfortunately due to the beast that is ue5 there's not really any promising direct assistance ai's that I've personally seen(I would love to be proved wrong tho), there are ones appearing for unity and godot(I've been playing around with the orca engine that you may see mentioned). Honestly it might be worth doing a bit of c++ studying for when a decent one comes out so that you can work with it and in the meantime try out the assistance ai's for godot and unity

replies.author: TheHoppingGroundhog
replies.body: i have a 7800 XT (with 16GB VRAM) and 32GB DDR4, will that run Qwen3 well?

replies.author: Katwazere
replies.body: Yes. You can run the quantized 7b version of it. Ollama is the most simple software for running llms locally so I recommend that

comments.author: ValleyOfWalls
comments.body:
I’ve been using cursor with sonnet 4, which works. There’s a trial, but yeah, you’re probably going to need a subscription. You could use the free web version of Claude and copy over code, but it’s a pain and you’ll also hit a debilitating frequency of rate limits. 

You will still want to learn ue5 blueprints, and I recommend you at minimum understand the use cases for the standard ue5 classes (gamemode, gamestate, player state, player controller, etc.) before asking any ai tool to go wild.

comments.author: isrichards6
comments.body:
If you're just trying to use AI as a learning tool Gemini 2.5 Pro is free if you use Google's AI Studio, it's better than any paid web based model you can use. You have to manually give it context of your project but that's as easy as dragging files and taking screenshots.

That being said I think Unreal Engine is a bad starting point for any new game developer.

replies.author: isrichards6
replies.body:
Unity is much easier to learn with as someone who's learned with both. There's a lot less going on so there's not as many systems you need to know before you can get a solid game together. C# in general is much easier to pick up and understand. There's way more learning resources out there in case you get stuck. Unreals documentation really sucks so you have to be comfortable combing source code to figure things out sometimes.

Even if you rely heavily on AI there will be points you get stuck and this is where you'll really feel the difference.

replies.author: Still_Ad9431
replies.body: Unity has their own AI, so you don't need to use AI

replies.author: moneydollarz
replies.body: Yeah but you have to buy the Unity subscription to use their ai

replies.author: Microtom_
replies.body: You can totally do it. I use ue5 and free Gemini 2.5 pro on aistudio to program in c++. My game has 20k lines of working code and I don't even know anything.

comments.author: littleboymark
comments.body: I'd get Claude Code, Windsurf, or Cursor. I use them all and they're relatively inexpensive and highly capable for all game development needs.

comments.author: Still_Ad9431
comments.body: Chatgpt could text to Blueprints tho.

comments.author: rakanssh
comments.body:
You can make an account on https://openrouter.ai it's mainly for API access but they do have a decent Chat UI that's usable. Open router lists providers and some of them are free (There's deepseek r1/3.1, kimi k2, and a few others).

You'll be limited tp 50 requests per day but if you charge 10$ once the limit is 1k per day. Be warned though, open router states that free providers collect your prompts and use them for training, so 0 identifiable information. This isn't the case for paid providers.

You can also use those credits to chat with any model at API prices, or even use any chat client like [webui](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui) and connect it to your open router account to have a ChatGPT like client for all models there, free or paid. Or connect it to an IDE with the many extensions out there.

Even if you pay it might be cheaper than subscriptions especially if you only use it occasionally, you'd be paying just for what you use.

comments.author: Ok-Visual-5862
comments.body: Any time I ask AI for help with C++ it hallucinates imaginary source code, functions, and variables that don't exist. Good luck.

comments.author: Appropriate-Tap7860
comments.body:
One thing that worked for me was converting blueprints code to c++. You can copy the bp nodes and paste it in ASCII format in chat gpt and ask it to convert to c++.
This is the only instance where it works without hallucination 95% of the time
